14	// pushShouldReveal reports whether the pre-push progress line should be shown:
15	// only when styled (ANSI-capable per interactive.ShouldStyle — respects
16	// NO_COLOR and TERM=cygwin, not merely "stderr is a terminal"), and only once
17	// the push has run long enough to feel stuck.
18	func pushShouldReveal(elapsed, threshold time.Duration, styled bool) bool {
19		return styled && elapsed >= threshold
20	}
21	
22	// pushReporter is a threshold-gated, single-in-place-line progress reporter
23	// for the pre-push checkpoint sync. It always logs to file via logging.Debug,
24	// but only writes to its terminal writer once the push has run long enough to
25	// feel stuck (and never at all when styled is false) — agents and CI must see
26	// zero bytes.
27	type pushReporter struct {
28		ctx       context.Context
29		w         io.Writer
30		styled    bool
31		threshold time.Duration
32		start     time.Time
33	
34		mu       sync.Mutex
35		revealed bool
36		prefix   string
37		detail   string
38	
39		done    chan struct{}
40		stopped chan struct{}
41	}
42	
43	// newPushReporter creates a pushReporter and starts its background reveal
44	// goroutine. Callers must call finish to stop the goroutine and print the
45	// persistent summary line.
46	func newPushReporter(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, styled bool, threshold time.Duration) *pushReporter {
47		r := &pushReporter{
48			ctx:       ctx,
49			w:         w,
50			styled:    styled,
51			threshold: threshold,
52			start:     time.Now(),
53			done:      make(chan struct{}),
54			stopped:   make(chan struct{}),
55		}
56		go r.run()
57		return r
58	}
59	
60	// run waits until the threshold elapses, then ticks ~1s, redrawing the
61	// in-place line while the reporter is not yet done.
62	func (r *pushReporter) run() {
63		defer close(r.stopped)
64	
65		timer := time.NewTimer(r.threshold)
66		defer timer.Stop()
67	
68		select {
69		case <-r.done:
70			return
71		case <-timer.C:
72		}
73	
74		r.mu.Lock()
75		r.maybeReveal()
76		r.mu.Unlock()
77	
78		ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Second)
79		defer ticker.Stop()
80	
81		for {
82			select {
83			case <-r.done:
84				return
85			case <-ticker.C:
86				r.mu.Lock()
87				r.maybeReveal()
88				r.mu.Unlock()
89			}
90		}
91	}
92	
93	// maybeReveal writes the current in-place line when reveal conditions are
94	// met. Callers must hold r.mu.
95	func (r *pushReporter) maybeReveal() {
96		if !pushShouldReveal(time.Since(r.start), r.threshold, r.styled) {
97			return
98		}
99		r.revealed = true
100		r.redrawLocked()
101	}
102	
103	// redrawLocked writes the current in-place line. Callers must hold r.mu.
104	func (r *pushReporter) redrawLocked() {
105		if !r.styled {
106			return
107		}
108		elapsed := int(time.Since(r.start).Seconds())
109		if r.detail != "" {
110			fmt.Fprintf(r.w, "\r[entire] %s… %s (%ds)\033[K", r.prefix, r.detail, elapsed)
111		} else {
112			fmt.Fprintf(r.w, "\r[entire] %s… (%ds)\033[K", r.prefix, elapsed)
113		}
114	}

116	// phase sets the current prefix text (e.g. "syncing 12 checkpoints"). It
117	// always logs to file; if the line is already revealed, it redraws
118	// immediately.
119	func (r *pushReporter) phase(prefix string) {
120		logging.Debug(r.ctx, "checkpoint push progress", slog.String("phase", prefix))
121	
122		r.mu.Lock()
123		defer r.mu.Unlock()
124		r.prefix = prefix
125		if r.revealed {
126			r.redrawLocked()
127		}
128	}
129	
130	// setDetail updates the live transfer detail (e.g. "writing 40/47 objects")
131	// shown alongside the prefix, redrawing immediately if the line is already
132	// revealed. Deliberately does not log to file on every call — it is driven by
133	// git's --progress stream, which ticks far more often than is useful in the
134	// debug log; logGitProgress records the transfer detail to file once, after
135	// the push completes.
136	func (r *pushReporter) setDetail(detail string) {
137		r.mu.Lock()
138		defer r.mu.Unlock()
139		r.detail = detail
140		if r.revealed {
141			r.redrawLocked()
142		}
143	}
144	
145	// finish stops the reveal goroutine and, if the line was ever revealed,
146	// prints a PERSISTENT final summary line (trailing newline, so it stays in
147	// the user's scrollback rather than being erased) and logs the final summary
148	// to file. Stays completely silent when the line was never revealed —
149	// agents/CI/fast pushes must see zero bytes.
150	func (r *pushReporter) finish(summary string) {
151		close(r.done)
152		<-r.stopped
153	
154		r.mu.Lock()
155		if r.revealed && r.styled {
156			if summary == "" {
157				// No summary (e.g. an aborted/failed push whose caller prints its
158				// own error next): just clear the in-place line, don't emit a
159				// content-less "[entire]  (Ns)" persistent line.
160				fmt.Fprint(r.w, "\r\033[K")
161			} else {
162				elapsed := int(time.Since(r.start).Seconds())
163				fmt.Fprintf(r.w, "\r[entire] %s (%ds)\033[K\n", summary, elapsed)
164			}
165		}
166		r.mu.Unlock()
167	
168		logging.Debug(r.ctx, "checkpoint push finished", slog.String("summary", summary))
169	}

26	// partitionLocalRefs splits refs into those that exist locally (pushable) and
27	// those that don't (stale queue entries — e.g. a checkpoint ref deleted by
28	// cleanup). Stale refs can never push, so callers drop them from the queue
29	// rather than retrying them forever.
30	func partitionLocalRefs(repo *git.Repository, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName) (existing, stale []plumbing.ReferenceName) {
31		for _, ref := range refs {
32			_, err := repo.Reference(ref, false)
33			switch {
34			case err == nil:
35				existing = append(existing, ref)
36			case errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound):
37				// Genuinely gone (e.g. deleted by cleanup) — never pushable, drop it.
38				stale = append(stale, ref)
39			default:
40				// A transient/IO lookup error: keep the ref as pushable so a real
41				// entry isn't dropped from the queue forever over a flaky read.
42				existing = append(existing, ref)
43			}
44		}
45		return existing, stale
46	}

48	// batchPushRefs pushes all of refs to target in a single git push,
49	// fast-forward-only (NOT a force push). Batching keeps a backfill of many refs to
50	// one network round-trip. Per-checkpoint refs normally advance by fast-forward
51	// (each write parents on the prior tip), so the common case succeeds; a
52	// non-fast-forward update — genuine divergence, e.g. the same checkpoint written
53	// differently on another machine — is REJECTED rather than silently overwriting
54	// the remote. We deliberately do not force: there is no server-side ref
55	// protection, so a force push would make a buggy or racing client clobber good
56	// remote history with no signal. On rejection the whole push errors; the caller
57	// retries the rejected refs individually with fetch+replay recovery
58	// (pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery).
59	// progressW, when non-nil, receives a live copy of git's --progress stderr
60	// bytes as the push runs (see remote.PushOptions.ProgressWriter) — typically a
61	// *gitProgressStreamer feeding a pushReporter's setDetail. Pass nil when no
62	// caller needs live streaming (e.g. the single-ref recovery retry).
63	func batchPushRefs(ctx context.Context, target string, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName, progressW io.Writer) error {
64		if len(refs) == 0 {
65			return nil
66		}
67		refSpecs := make([]string, 0, len(refs))
68		for _, ref := range refs {
69			refSpecs = append(refSpecs, ref.String()+":"+ref.String())
70		}
71		result, err := remote.PushWithOptions(ctx, remote.PushOptions{Remote: target, RefSpecs: refSpecs, ProgressWriter: progressW})
72		logGitProgress(ctx, result.Stderr)
73		if err != nil {
74			return fmt.Errorf("push %d checkpoint refs: %w", len(refs), err)
75		}
76		return nil
77	}

79	// pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery pushes a single checkpoint ref fast-forward-only;
80	// on rejection — typically the ref diverged on the remote (the same checkpoint
81	// re-written elsewhere) — it fetches the remote ref and replays the local-only
82	// commits on top via fetchAndRebaseRefCommon, then retries. The retry is still
83	// non-force: after the replay the local ref is a fast-forward over the remote, so
84	// the remote commit is preserved as an ancestor rather than overwritten. The
85	// cherry-pick is delta-based, so non-overlapping changes merge; a genuine overlap
86	// (e.g. both sides rewrote the root metadata.json) surfaces as a rebase error and
87	// the ref is left for a later pre-push. Returns nil only if the ref reached the
88	// remote.
89	func pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
90		// One shared budget across the initial push, fetch+replay, and retry, matching
91		// doPushRef (fetchAndRebaseRefCommon relies on the caller's deadline).
92		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointPushBudget)
93		defer cancel()

95		if err := batchPushRefs(ctx, target, []plumbing.ReferenceName{ref}, nil); err == nil {
96			return nil
97		}

99			return fmt.Errorf("sync diverged checkpoint ref %s: %w", ref, err)
100		}
101		return batchPushRefs(ctx, target, []plumbing.ReferenceName{ref}, nil)
102	}

104	// pushRefIfNeeded pushes a ref to the given target if it has unpushed changes.
105	// The target can be a remote name (e.g., "origin") or a URL for direct push.
106	// For branch refs, the "has unpushed" optimization consults the remote-tracking
107	// ref. Non-branch refs and URL targets skip the optimization and let git
108	// handle the no-op case.
109	// Does not check any settings — callers are responsible for gating.
110	func pushRefIfNeeded(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
111		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
112		if err != nil {
113			logging.Debug(ctx, "push skipped: open repository failed",
114				slog.String("ref", ref.String()),
115				slog.String("error", err.Error()))

120		localRef, err := repo.Reference(ref, true)

123			return nil
124		}

126		if ref.IsBranch() && !remote.IsURL(target) && !hasUnpushedBranchRef(repo, target, localRef.Hash(), ref.Short()) {

133	// hasUnpushedBranchRef checks if the local branch differs from the remote.
134	// Returns true if there's any difference that needs syncing (local ahead, remote ahead, or diverged).
135	func hasUnpushedBranchRef(repo *git.Repository, remoteName string, localHash plumbing.Hash, branchName string) bool {
136		// Check for remote tracking ref: refs/remotes/<remoteName>/<branch>
137		remoteRefName := plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(remoteName, branchName)
138		remoteRef, err := repo.Reference(remoteRefName, true)
139		if err != nil {
140			// Remote branch doesn't exist yet - we have content to push
141			return true
142		}
143	
144		// If local and remote point to same commit, nothing to sync
145		// This is the only case where we skip - any difference needs handling
146		return localHash != remoteRef.Hash()
147	}

157	// (the git-branch legacy backend's phased "Pushing/Syncing/done" output and
158	// the session-tree summary). Always resolves os.Stderr at call time so tests
159	// can redirect stderr. Resolves to io.Discard when stderr isn't a real

177	// doPushRef pushes the given ref to the target with fetch+rebase recovery.

179	func doPushRef(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
180		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointPushBudget)

185		displayTarget := displayPushTarget(target)

189		pushStart := time.Now()
190	
191		result, err := tryPushRefCommon(ctx, target, ref)

198		// actionable error, not progress — always print it, even on non-TTY
199		// stderr, so it bypasses the gated pushProgressOutput() writer.
200		var protectedErr *protectedRefError
201		if errors.As(err, &protectedErr) {
202			printProtectedRefBlock(os.Stderr, refLabel, target)
203			return nil
204		}

207		// fetch+rebase, and retrying would just reprint the same opaque error.
208		// Surface an actionable ssh-agent hint and skip recovery (issue #1523).

245				printNonInteractiveSSHAuthHint()
246			}
